<Rep. Robert C. "Bobby" Scott, Rep. Suzanne Bonamici, Rep. Alma S. Adams, Rep. Mark DeSaulnier, Rep. Jahana Hayes, Rep. Summer L. Lee>: Introduction
H.R. 3495, the Direct Seller and Real Estate Agent Harmonization Act, would amend federal wage-and-hour law so that people who work in commissioned sales (including real estate agents and salespersons in multi-level marketing businesses) and newspaper delivery workers are excluded from the definition of an employee entitled to wage-and-hour protections. The law that would be changed by this bill--the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938\1\ (FLSA)--already accommodates the industries' customary commission-based pay practices. By categorically excluding these occupations from FLSA, this bill would threaten the independence of legitimate independent contractors and imperil the protections of low-wage workers in call centers. The Committee has not conducted any hearings on whether there is a problem to be fixed in these industries or any potential downstream consequences of the changes this bill could create.
\1\Pub. L. No. 75-718, 52 Stat. 1060 (1938).
This bill is opposed by the Communication Workers of America and the National Employment Lawyers Association.
Background on Direct Sellers and Real Estate Agents
The short title of H.R. 3495 draws attention to two categories of workers: direct sellers and real estate agents. Direct Sellers
The direct selling business model is predicated on direct sales of products and services outside of a traditional retail setting.\2\ Today, a prominent form of direct selling is multi-level marketing (MLM). In an MLM business model, a company
\2\Johanna Leggatt, Understanding Multi-Level Marketing, Forbes (Apr. 11, 2025), https://www.forbes.com/advisor/investing/multi-level-marketing-mlm/.
distributes products or services through a network of
participants. Typically, the company does not directly
recruit new participants, but relies on its existing
participants to recruit additional participants, who,
in turn, also recruit new participants. This creates
multiple levels of participants organized in
``downlines.'' A participant's ``downline'' is the
network of their recruits, and recruits of those
recruits, and so on. A participant's ``upline'' is the
person who recruited them, and the person who recruited
their recruiter, and so on.\3\
\3\Business Guidance Concerning Multi-Level Marketing, Fed. Trade Comm., https://www.ftc.gov/business-guidance/resources/business-guidance-concerning-multi-level-marketing (last visited Sept. 26, 2025).
Some notable MLM companies include Amway, Herbalife, and Mary Kay.\4\ Although not necessarily illegal by definition, ``many MLMs have become infamous for their controversial business practices.''\5\ MLM businesses ``tend to appeal to new recruits with promises of wealth and independence,''\6\ but ``it's the [MLM] company that hoards most of the advantages of the arrangement: an individual direct seller receives no salary, benefits, or paid time off; does not set her own prices or sales goals; has no say on suppliers or marketing strategy; and generally does not even choose what products she is selling.''\7\
\4\Peter Gratton, What Is MLM? How Multilevel Marketing or Network Marketing Works, Investopedia (May 14, 2025), https:// www.investopedia.com/terms/m/multi-level-marketing.asp.
\5\See Leggatt, supra note 2.
\6\Id.
\7\Jessica Winter, The Unkillable Appeal of Multilevel Marketing, The New Yorker (Mar. 20, 2024), https://www.newyorker.com/books/under-review/the-unkillable-appeal-of-multilevel-marketing.
Real Estate Agents
Real estate agents are licensed professionals who help clients buy, sell, and manage real estate.\8\ They are overwhelmingly--87% nationwide, according to the National Association of Realtors (NAR)\9\--set up as independent contractors and are customarily paid on a commission basis rather than a regular wage.\10\
\8\Occupational Outlook Handbook: Real Estate Brokers and Sales Agents, Bureau of Lab. Stats. (Aug. 28, 2025), https://www.bls.gov/ooh/ sales/real-estate-brokers-and-sales-agents.htm.
\9\NAR Issue Brief: Real Estate Professionals Classification as Independent Contractors, Nat'l Ass'n of Realtors (Jan. 10, 2024), https://www.nar.realtor/advocacy/nar-issue-brief-real-estate-professionals-classification-as-independent-contractors [hereinafter NAR Brief].
\10\Victoria Araj, Real Estate Broker vs. Agent: Differences Explained, Rocket Mortgage (Jan. 13, 2025), https:// www.rocketmortgage.com/learn/real-estate-broker-vs-agent.
Real estate agents are required under state laws to affiliate with a licensed real estate broker, who is also a licensed professional able to do the same work as an agent as well as move money to and from escrow accounts, mediate conflicts over transactions, and ensure legal compliance for real estate transactions that they and their affiliated agents close.\11\ Real estate brokers typically earn commissions for transactions they close themselves and receive a portion of the commission earned by real estate agents affiliated with them.\12\
\11\Lauren Bowling, What Is a Real Estate Broker and What Do They Do?, Rocket Mortgage (Feb. 2, 2024), https://www.rocketmortgage.com/ learn/real-estate-broker.
\12\Id.
Real estate agents are generally limited to affiliating with only one broker in a state, although they may be able to affiliate with brokers in other states for purposes of arranging real estate transactions across state lines.\13\
\13\Carlton, FAQ: Can a Real Estate Agent Work for Multiple Brokers?, Realty Hub (June 26, 2025), https://joinrealtyhub.com/can-a-real-estate-agent-work-for-multiple-brokers/.
Upstream Power Players
Whether or not a direct seller or real estate agent works as an employee or an independent contractor, each is subject to some sort of supervision or set of rules determined by a powerful actor. That actor can be a branded MLM firm, the ``upline'' lineage of sellers who collect a percentage of a seller's commissions,\14\ or a real estate broker, as the case may be. For convenience, we will refer to these entities collectively as upstream power players.
\14\See supra text accompanying note 3.
Employment Law This Bill Would Amend
H.R. 3495 would change the definition of employee in the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 (FLSA). FLSA is the federal employment law governing the minimum wage,\15\ overtime,\16\ oppressive child labor,\17\ discrimination in pay on the basis of sex,\18\ and the right of nursing mothers to take paid breaks at work for the purpose of expressing breast milk.\19\ It is enforced by the Wage and Hour Division (WHD) of the U.S. Department of Labor (DOL), as well as by workers themselves who bring cases in court.
\15\FLSA Sec. 6.
\16\Id. Sec. 7.
\17\Id. Sec. 12.
\18\Id. Sec. 6(d).
\19\Id. Sec. 18D.
Economic Realities Test
In FLSA, the term ``employ'' includes ``to suffer or permit to work.''\20\ Courts test the applicability of the FLSA definition using the ``economic realities'' test, which looks underneath whatever terms the parties to a relationship use to describe it and focuses instead on the reality of the relationship. The economic realities test examines the facts of the working relationship in light of the totality of the circumstances to determine whether the putative employee is economically dependent on the potential employer.\21\ Ultimately, the application of the economic realities factors is guided by the overarching principle that the FLSA should be ``construed liberally to apply to the furthest reaches consistent with congressional direction.''\22\
\20\Id. Sec. 3(g).
\21\Tony & Susan Alamo Found. v. Sec'y of Labor, 471 U.S. 290, 301
(1985) (reiterating that the test of employment under the FLSA is economic reality); Goldberg v. Whitaker House Co-op, Inc., 366 U.S. 28, 33 (1961).
\22\Mitchell v. Lublin, McGaughy & Assocs., 358 U.S. 207 (1959).
The FLSA definitions of ``employ'' and ``employee'' also apply to family and medical leave rights under the Family and Medical Leave Act of 1993 (FMLA).\23\
\23\Pub. L. No. 103-3, Sec. 101(2)(C) (1993).
Relevant Exemptions
Even with its broad reach, FLSA still accommodates the particular needs and longstanding practices of specific industries and occupations, including a special rule for outside salespersons and another for news delivery persons.
The FLSA outside sales exemption excludes ``any employee employed . . . in the capacity of outside salesman'' from the minimum wage and overtime provisions of the law.\24\ WHD defines this exemption as applying to an employee (1) whose primary duty is making sales or obtaining orders or contracts for services or the use of facilities for which a client or customer will pay some consideration, and (2) who conducts this work customarily and regularly outside of a fixed place of business (including the employee's own home).\25\ This exemption covers a wide range of sales activity, including real estate, radio and TV time, print ads, and intellectual property.\26\
\24\FLSA Sec. 13(a)(1).
\25\29 C.F.R. Sec. Sec. 541.500-504.
\26\Wage & Hr. Div., U.S. Dep't of Lab., Fact Sheet #17: Exemption for Outside Sales Employees Under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) (Aug. 2024).
The FLSA news delivery exemption excludes ``any employee engaged in the delivery of newspapers to the consumer'' from minimum wage, overtime, equal pay, and child labor provisions.\27\
\27\FLSA Sec. 13(d).
How FLSA Would Be Amended
H.R. 3495 would amend the definition of employee in FLSA by excluding any worker treated for purposes of federal tax law as a statutory non-employee in section 3508 of the Internal Revenue Code.
Section 3508 allows, for purposes of tax treatment, that workers will be deemed independent contractors if they satisfy the following:
(1) They are either licensed real estate agents or
engaged in multi-level marketing/direct sales (e.g.,
Amway, Avon, Tupperware), trade or sales of consumer
products in the home or anywhere other than a retail
establishment, or engaged in newspaper or shopping news
delivery or distribution;
(2) Substantially all remuneration is directly
related to sales or other output rather than the number
of hours worked; and
(3) Services are performed pursuant to a contract
establishing the non-employee nature of the
relationship.
There is substantial overlap with the FLSA outside sales and news delivery exemptions, except that the tax code definition does not include FLSA's specification of sales work conducted primarily outside of fixed workplaces.
Weaknesses of H.R. 3495
No Established Problem
If there is a problem to be addressed by this bill, it has never been established in this Committee. No Committee hearing has been scheduled this Congress, or in any Congress in recent memory, to identify any cases at all in which the real estate, direct sales, or news delivery industries have been disrupted, upset, or even slightly bothered by application of FLSA employment rules.
In fact, even if a real estate agent or direct seller could make a case that an employment relationship had been established in a given set of circumstances, the outside sales and news delivery exemptions already bar the application of minimum wage and overtime rules, allowing for the longstanding commission-oriented pay practices of those industries to prevail (even where, as is often the case in MLM businesses, sellers wind up earning less than the minimum wage or just drown in red ink).\28\
\28\Michelle, Singletary, Why Multilevel Marketing Won't Make You Rich, Wash. Post (Sept. 26, 2018), https://www.washingtonpost.com/ business/2018/09/27/why-that-multilevel-marketing-business-is-probably-not-going-pay-off/.
The Same Wrong Song and Dance
In the absence of committee hearings on the matter, the only resource for the case in favor of this legislation comes from the groups lobbying for it. They appear, however, to fundamentally misunderstand the relevant law and recent rulemakings implementing it.
